question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (Cat III AIF, determinate trust) sold STT-paid listed equity shares held for 18 months. Gross LTCG for the financial year is INR 10.25 lakh. Using the post-Budget 2024 rate under Section 112A and applying the INR 1.25 lakh exemption, what is the fund-level LTCG tax (ignoring surcharge and cess, pure 12.5% slab)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Taxable LTCG = 10,25,000 − 1,25,000 exemption = 9,00,000. LTCG tax = 9,00,000 × 12.5% = INR 1,12,500. Budget 2024 raised the 112A rate from 10% to 12.5% and the exemption threshold from INR 1 lakh to INR 1.25 lakh with effect from 23-07-2024. The Trap: INR 1,28,125 applies 12.5% to the whole 10.25L without the 1.25L exemption. INR 1,02,500 uses the old 10% rate post-exemption. INR 1,25,000 ignores the 25% uplift in rate post-Budget 2024. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests the same calc from investor-communication angle. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) uses it for PMS clients. XIX-E focuses on the fund-level treatment because Section 115UB does not route the gain to LPs. Manager's Pro-Tip: At Nilgiri, the INR 1.25 lakh exemption is a fund-level quirk — a single large LTCG print wipes it out. Stagger exits across FY only if deferring capital materially helps; otherwise realise in-window and account for 12.5% + surcharge (capped at 15% for LTCG/STCG) + 4% cess in NAV.
